title: "Python and CLI API"
description: "Stable entry points, report schemas, and lower-level mathematical functions."
---

## High-level API

### `budget(d, m, q=None, spectrum=None)`

Returns a `BudgetReport` with exact isotropic laws and optional spectrum-aware
diagnostics. `to_dict()` is JSON serializable and conforms to
`schemas/budget-report.schema.json`.

### `audit(X, m, q=10, n_trials=2000, rng=None)`

Returns an `AuditReport`. Rows of `X` are observations. Randomness is entirely
controlled by the supplied NumPy generator.

### `recommend_dimension(d, **targets)`

Returns the smallest `m < d` meeting all targets. Available targets are
`hgr_capacity`, `pairwise_agreement`, `kendall_tau`, `nearest_neighbor`, and
`shape_information`. Set `q` for a nearest-neighbor target.

## Command line

```text
rpgeom budget --d D --m M [--q Q] [--spectrum FILE] [--json]
rpgeom recommend --d D [TARGET OPTIONS] [--json]
rpgeom audit MATRIX --m M [--q Q] [--trials N] [--seed S] [--json]
rpgeom verify [--full]
rpgeom reproduce-paper [--full] [--output DIR]
```

## Mathematical modules

- `rpgeom.ceilings`: HGR, spectral recovery shares, Laguerre modes, information ratios.
- `rpgeom.laws`: pairwise, Kendall, plurality, and coupling laws.
- `rpgeom.channels`: beta–gamma samples and exact-moment polynomial CCA.
- `rpgeom.maps`: Haar frames, Gaussian stages, and chains.
- `rpgeom.ensembles`: stacking, averaging, condition-number, and alignment diagnostics.
- `rpgeom.mmse`: noisy singular-direction recovery and hard-edge examples.
- `rpgeom.plotting`: reusable publication plotting defaults.

All public numerical functions reject invalid dimensions instead of silently
returning NaNs. Array inputs require finite values.
